report:
PASS applies to the entire asserted partial theorem, relative to the supplied complete B grant. It does not close original P16.4. No material mathematical defect or essential unverified dependency remains in the boundary argument.

The task-authority passage is: “The ONLY caller mathematical grant is the ENTIRE accepted original P16.5 body B, solely in its smooth integral projective algebraically closed trivially valued characteristic-zero actual-big rational-line-bundle domain.” Source: urn:xean:task. This task-granted assumption is excluded from the external-premises array. B is not a registered native-note support ID, and its internal G0/G1 references confer no additional domain.

The established scope is every characteristic-zero field with trivial absolute value, every smooth geometrically integral projective variety over it, and every actual ample rational line bundle. The construction covers the full analytic carrier, arbitrary finite-energy measure support, arbitrary decreasing nets, and supported poles. It gives the genuine mixed E1 operator of raw mass V=(L^n), its energy and weighted continuity, compactness, envelopes, both-sign outer differentiation, locality, comparison, attainment, and uniqueness for every solution. The exact targets are positive Radon measures of mass V with finite continuous-test dual energy, equivalently measures integrating every actual E1 potential. The dimension-zero statement also holds.

The fixed-bundle bridge is valid. For each positive rational t, numerical openness makes the actual difference L−(1−t)B_i ample on a sufficiently late tail. Tensoring with its weight-zero generators preserves the scalar at every valuation-ring center, including nongeneric support. Appending the generated floor produces a basepoint-free system on the actual L. Eligible triples have common refinements, and h_i−C≤0 gives the required monotonicity as t decreases. Their infimum is u everywhere; finite thresholds prove the assertion at poles. Thus B’s varying-bundle ample cone really equals the fixed-bundle cone used by the paper. No numerical replacement of L is made.

The analytic quotient proof handles all fibers. At a finite Galois level, H(x)⊗k E is a nonzero finite étale algebra, hence a product of finite separable fields. Complete-field uniqueness supplies exactly one norm on each factor. An orbit of factors would give an invariant idempotent; the invariant algebra is H(x), so the action is transitive. Compatible finite-coefficient seminorms reconstruct the algebraic-closure analytification. The finite-intersection argument in the profinite group then identifies each full fiber with one orbit. Finite coefficients also establish joint continuity. Geometric integrality makes k(X)⊗k E a field, and its extended trivial norm is trivial; consequently the generic fiber is a singleton. The finite-extension norm statement and its proof were checked in [Sharifi, §5.4](https://www.math.ucla.edu/~sharifi/notes/algnum-ch05.html). No completed nontrivially valued closure is involved.

Actual FS descent is sound. The conjugate section list has a finite semilinearly stable weighted flag. Uniqueness of reduced row echelon form puts its matrices over k. An adapted k-basis reproduces the same weighted maximum: each expression uses vectors of at least the relevant weight, and every nonzero coefficient has norm one. Both ultrametric inequalities remain valid at section zeros. Faithful flatness preserves generation. For singular endpoints, the compact closed orbit-superlevel sets prove that the decreasing orbit maxima have precisely the original invariant endpoint, including −∞. This justifies the arbitrary-net descent; it does not exchange an unrestricted supremum with an infimum. Continuous endpoints give uniform convergence by the compact-superlevel Dini argument.

The invariant Radon lift is correctly constructed and unique. Finite-quotient probability averages approximate the Haar functional, uniformly for a continuous function composed with the compact group action. Averaging descends continuous tests, and the positive functional on C(Y) gives a Radon measure with unchanged mass. Every invariant measure integrates a test exactly as it integrates its average, so its pushforward determines it. This also proves the weak-topology assertions. Subsequent Borel integral identities are ordinary single-measure pushforward identities. A finite orbit of r points receives weight 1/r at each point; this is the stabilizer quotient, and r need not be the extension degree.

The continuous operator agreement and raw normalization check out. Constant separable extension is étale at the relevant central DVRs, preserving b_Q and the normalized valuations. Projection contributes [E:k], while conversion from k-degrees to E-degrees cancels that factor. Summing split components therefore preserves each pushed coefficient and V. The finite model coefficient law was checked through the complete pertinent units of [Chambert-Loir–Ducros v1, §§6.4 and 6.9](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1204.6277v1). Its use concerns continuous finite models only. Rational FS coefficients agree with B; rational approximation of real weights and decreasing shifted uniform FS approximants then identify the continuous limits. Checked [Boucksom–Eriksson v3](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1805.01016v3) units include §4.1, 5.17–18, 7.2–14, 8.3–6, and 9.13–14, with their pertinent proofs. The nontrivial-valuation hypothesis of its Theorem 7.8 is not used for trivial fields.

Singular energy equality has both inequalities. Continuous base psh majorants pull back to permissible upstairs majorants. Conversely, actual descended FS majorants decrease to u, and their equal continuous energies decrease to B’s energy, including when the limit is −∞. This establishes energy cofinality without assuming that averaging a majorant lowers energy. Equation (12) therefore defines the actual mixed operator before any target is considered. Transport of sections and intersections, followed by continuous and decreasing limits, establishes G-equivariance. Invariant upstairs outputs are exactly the unique lifts of their pushed outputs. B’s genuine integrability, mixed and weighted decreasing continuity, and energy identity consequently descend through the exact integral law.

Algebraic intermediate fields are treated correctly. For every algebraic F/k, including infinite and non-Galois extensions, Gal(kbar/F) gives the appropriate quotient and the same energy construction. Composition of pushforwards proves (14). For non-Galois F, the distinguished lift is obtained from the G-invariant measure upstairs; no transitivity assertion about Aut(F/k) is made. Changing algebraic closure transports the construction. Reference covariance follows from the continuous energy cocycle and the bijection of absolute majorants: E_a(u−a)=E_0(u)−E_0(a), and the dual energy changes by −E_0(a)+∫a dμ, a finite correction.

The divisorial topology argument is valid. An upstairs divisorial coordinate descends to a finite constant extension; restriction retains a discrete rank-one group and residue transcendence degree n−1. Conversely, finite constant extension of a base DVR is étale. At a prime above its closed point, the reduced residue algebra shows that the original uniformizer still generates the maximal ideal, giving ramification index one. This is the scope needed from [Stacks, Tag 0AP2](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0AP2). Algebraic realization and characteristic-zero resolution provide the required models; the applicable resolution/principalization statement and proof were checked in [Encinas–Hauser v1](https://arxiv.org/html/math/0211423v1). These are Noetherian models over fields, not resolutions over nondiscrete valuation rings. The resulting coordinate correspondence identifies the topologies. Divisorial equalities define a closed invariant locus, and B’s all-point determination promotes them to actual invariance. Thus the normalized potential cone and its energy-cost subsets are compact, rather than merely spaces of measures.

Envelope descent is all-point. The upstairs envelope of the invariant pulled obstacle is invariant because the group permutes its competitors. Psh descent and maximality give both inequalities in (15). Compact-group quotient maps are open, which also makes usc regularization commute with pullback. For ample L, B’s decomposition L=1·L+0 makes its model-envelope continuity locus the whole carrier; its Lipschitz envelope law and model density give continuity for continuous obstacles. This establishes the continuous-envelope property actually used in orthogonality.

Both signs of every continuous-direction outer derivative follow from energy equality, envelope equality, and B’s derivative in its granted ample domain. The perturbed envelopes lie between u±|t|‖h‖, so remain E1. For affine E1 segments, B’s mixed polynomial identity passes through pushforward; all coefficients integrate the fixed difference v−u. The energy identity then gives the stated endpoint and interior derivatives. This uses genuine mixed measures, not multilinearity of big positive products. Orthogonality follows from the constant-envelope path P(a+t(f−a))=a and its right derivative. Strict locality and comparison push through the literal inverse images of the Borel winner sets. Integrability supplies the common full-measure finite-value sets; no pole subtraction is required.

The directed Radon integration argument is correct. For increasing nonnegative continuous functions, a strict superlevel of their supremum is a union of open stage superlevels. Each inner compact subset has a finite subcover, and directedness supplies one dominating stage. Inner regularity, finite level partitions, and truncation prove equality of the supremum integral and the directed supremum of integrals. Applying this to C−v_i, together with decreasing finite energy, identifies the continuous-test and E1-test dual suprema and proves integrability when J is finite. This argument would not justify monotone convergence for arbitrary measurable nets; the paper does not make that substitution.

The dual-energy equality is also valid. Only continuous upstairs potentials are Haar-averaged. Uniform finite convex approximations preserve psh, concavity and equivariance increase energy under averaging, and invariant measures preserve the integral. Actual psh descent therefore proves the reverse inequality in (18); pullback proves the other. For the converse using only base E1 tests, failure of a uniform integral bound on cost≤1 yields the decreasing convex series p_m. Its generic value remains zero, its cost remains≤1, and actual closure plus energy continuity gives an E1 endpoint. Sequential monotone convergence contradicts its integrability. With the resulting bound C and C_0=2^(n+1), B’s contraction gives I(u)≤C√(C_0B(u)) for B(u)>1. Hence the dual supremum is finite, bounded by max(C,C_0C²/4). No singular averaging is used.

Attainment and every-solution uniqueness are established. The target lift satisfies precisely B’s intrinsic condition. Its normalized B solution is invariant: every transform solves the same target equation, B’s every-solution uniqueness gives a constant, and the fixed generic point makes that constant zero. Actual psh and energy descent give an original E1 solution. B’s whole supporting plane proves that its descended objective attains the original variational supremum; base competitors pull back. For any two base solutions, their invariant upstairs outputs have the same pushforward. Unique invariant lifting makes them the same B target, so B’s uniqueness applies to both, and surjectivity gives equality modulo one constant downstairs. This does not assume that an arbitrary solution was produced by the construction.

The Q example is correct. The cubic has distinct affine roots and a smooth point at infinity; dx/y extends to a nonzero regular differential. Its product is smooth and geometrically integral and has nonzero regular one-forms, excluding a smooth projective toric surface. O_C(3O) is the plane hyperplane bundle, so the product polarization is ample. The fiber intersections give (3F_1+3F_2)²=18. The exceptional prime of the blowup at (O,O) supplies a genuine divisorial coordinate. B’s normalized coordinate bound descends, and E(u)≤0 gives J(18δ_z)≤18C_z. Thus the asserted divisorial-atom application has the required mass and energy condition.

The mathematical assertions in n1 and n2 have the same checked dependencies as the paper; their source ledger and provenance confer no authority. The reported scripts, sample grid values, hashes and build executions in n3 are not independently authenticated by the supplied text, which does not include the programs or their tree coefficients. They are expressly nonessential observations: none supplies an operator, descent lemma, or theorem premise. The finite orbit and convex-averaging identities used in the argument were reconstructed independently. Documentary retrieval confirms that [CD v2](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1204.6277v2) has 608 pages and that its inspected multiplier/convergence units retain continuity and local uniform convergence. [Pille–Schneider v2](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2209.04879v2) and the [synthetic v1 introduction](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2307.01697v1) remain scope diagnostics, not missing-operator grants or exhaustive contemporary literature claims.

Harmless corrections: n2’s reference to “n1’s complete B grant” should mean the task’s B grant. At poles, uniqueness must be written u=v+c, rather than evaluating u−v. Two source errata are harmless: BE Lemma 8.6 needs subtraction between its final curvature terms; Proposition 9.14’s Lipschitz proof uses constant shifts alongside monotonicity. No substantive repair of the manuscript argument is needed.

Original P16.4 remains open in this submission. Its nontrivially valued residual scope still lacks the asserted potential compactness, envelope/model regularity and orthogonality inputs, genuine full-mass unbounded mixed products and weighted limits, both-sign differentiation, comparison and original-space attainment, and any necessary singular descent through completed algebraic closure. The paper proves none of these there. This PASS concerns partial correctness only; candidate=false and the unchanged original completion criterion remain appropriate. No editor or source file was changed.

premises: For a complete non-Archimedean field K, including trivial valuation, projective K-schemes have compact Hausdorff analytification; affine points are multiplicative seminorms extending the absolute value of K, with pointwise topology.

Every finite algebraic extension F of a complete non-Archimedean field H has a unique absolute value extending that of H and is complete for it. If H is trivially valued, this extended absolute value is trivial.

For projective geometrically reduced X over a complete non-Archimedean field K, including trivial valuation, and semiample rational L, continuous psh metrics admit uniform approximation by rational weighted FS metrics and smooth semipositive metrics.

For projective geometrically reduced n-dimensional X over a complete non-Archimedean field K, including trivial valuation, continuous psh metrics on semiample rational bundles have positive symmetric multiadditive mixed Radon measures of mixed intersection mass; uniform metric convergence implies weak measure convergence, and complete field extension satisfies the pushforward law.

For projective geometrically reduced X over a complete non-Archimedean field K, including trivial valuation, and semiample rational L, continuous relative Monge–Ampère energy satisfies the cocycle identity, shifts by c(L^n) when c is added to its first metric, is (L^n)-Lipschitz for the sum of the two sup distances, and is invariant under complete field extension.

Let K be a complete discretely valued field of residue characteristic zero, normalized by v_K(π)=1, and X/K smooth projective of dimension n. For rational model metrics on ample L_i, relatively generated on a common normal projective flat K°-model with special fiber ∑b_Q Q, the continuous mixed measure has coefficient b_Q deg_Q(ℒ_1|Q⋯ℒ_n|Q) at ord_Q/b_Q and total mass (L_1⋯L_n).

If A is a discrete valuation ring with uniformizer t and B is a finite étale A-algebra, then at every prime q of B above the maximal ideal of A, B_q is a discrete valuation ring and t remains a uniformizer; the ramification index is one.

Every reduced quasi-projective variety over a characteristic-zero field admits projective resolution by smooth-center blowups in a smooth ambient variety. On a smooth quasi-projective variety over such a field, nonzero coherent ideals admit principalization with simple normal crossings. These constructions can be compatible with smooth morphisms and separable field extensions and equivariant for group actions.
